overview.problemStatement: The admin console stops at moderation: four dashboard counters, a fixed 30-day analytics window with four charts and no filters, a settings page that exposes attendee onboarding state, and no reporting, export, announcement, feedback, platform-configuration, or health surface. Operators cannot see what needs attention, slice demand by segment, produce a credible post-event report, broadcast to a segmented audience, triage user reports, or verify background jobs are healthy.
overview.proposedSolution: Rebuild /admin as an operator command center: a grouped shell with a shared page header and a Ctrl/Cmd+K command palette; a decision-ready dashboard with trend cards, an action queue, today-at-a-glance, and recent audit activity; an analytics workspace driven by one server-side filter object with period comparison, five new chart families, and data-table alternatives; and new modules for CSV export, reports, super-admin platform settings, broadcast announcements, a support and feedback inbox, and system health. Admin settings drops attendee-only fields. Every new mutation is role-checked, validated, audited, and rate-limited.
overview.targetAudience: Ivent admins and super admins. Secondary beneficiaries: organizers and sponsors who receive reports, and attendees who receive announcements.
assumptions: The existing console from admin-console-and-governance v1 remains the base; this feature modifies it in place rather than replacing Clerk sign-in, invite acceptance, or the audit primitive.
hasCompletedOnboarding, interests, and location are attendee concepts; admins never complete attendee onboarding, so the value is structurally meaningless in an admin context.
Resend is the only email transport; no new vendor is introduced.
No new third-party UI package is required; components/ui, Recharts, date-fns, lucide-react, and react-day-picker cover the approved visual budget.
Read-on-demand analytics remains acceptable at current volumes; indexes and bounded ranges are added so filtered queries do not scan whole collections.
The product is global: currency, country, and timezone come from platform settings with USD and UTC defaults, and no screen may hard-code naira or NG.
Feedback and announcement records are internal operational data retained until an explicit, audited deletion.
outOfScope: Online payments, refunds, payouts, and tax handling.
Editing event content from the admin console; events remain organizer-owned.
Granular per-permission roles beyond user, admin, and super_admin.
A warehouse, nightly aggregate pipeline, or external BI integration.
Live chat or third-party helpdesk integration; the feedback inbox is internal only.
Draft, scheduled, recurring, or templated broadcasts.
SIEM export or external observability integration.
Public API or webhooks for admin data.

userStories.title: Navigate a grouped, consistent console
userStories.want: navigation grouped by job and one consistent page header
userStories.benefit: I can find the right tool quickly and every screen reads as one product

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given any /admin route, the sidebar groups destinations under Overview, Audience, Events, Operations, Governance, and Personal, marks the active item with aria-current, collapses to a drawer below md, and is generated from one configuration; after a route change the drawer closes and focus returns to its trigger.
Given any admin page, it renders a header with title, a one-sentence purpose, a breadcrumb, and an optional primary-action slot; at a 360px viewport the header wraps without horizontal scrolling.

userStories.title: Reach anything from the keyboard
userStories.benefit: I can jump to a page, event, user, or registration without walking menus

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given I press Ctrl/Cmd+K anywhere inside /admin, a dialog opens with a labelled search input, trapped focus, and Esc closing it back to the invoking element; typing two or more characters returns grouped results for Pages, Users, Events, and Registrations that are keyboard-navigable, and Enter opens the highlighted destination.

Given fewer than two characters, the palette shows only static page actions; given no matches, it names the query in an empty state; given a query failure, it shows an inline retry affordance rather than a blank panel.

userStories.title: Open the console to a decision, not a data dump
userStories.want: the dashboard to tell me what changed and what needs action

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given /admin/dashboard, I see trend cards for users, events, registrations, and estimated revenue, each with the comparison window named, a delta, and a sparkline; a zero or missing baseline renders new or no change instead of NaN, Infinity, or 0%.

Given pending operational items such as invites expiring within 48 hours, events at or above capacity, feedback open longer than 48 hours, and failed email deliveries, I see an action queue with counts and a link to each module; with none, the queue shows a positive empty state rather than an empty box.

Given I open the dashboard, I see today's events with check-in progress, the ten most recent audit entries with actor and relative time, and quick actions; each block has its own loading, empty, and error state.

userStories.title: Filter analytics by time and dimension
userStories.want: to slice analytics by time and dimensions
userStories.benefit: I can answer questions about one segment instead of the whole platform

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the analytics page, I can pick a 7/30/90/365-day preset or a custom range; the range is encoded in the URL, survives reload and back/forward, and one filter set drives every summary card and chart on the page.

Given filters for category, country, city, ticket type, organizer, registration status, and check-in state, I can combine them; active filters render as removable chips plus Clear all, and both the result count and the empty state reflect the filtered dataset.
Given a custom range whose start is after its end, or a span longer than 730 days, the page rejects it with an inline message and keeps the last valid query.

userStories.title: Compare a period with its predecessor
userStories.benefit: I can say whether growth is real

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given comparison is enabled, every summary metric shows the current value, previous value, absolute delta, percentage delta, and a direction indicator that is not conveyed by colour alone; when the previous value is zero, the delta renders new instead of a percentage.
Given comparison is disabled, no delta or ghost series renders, and the toggle state is preserved for the session.

userStories.title: See the funnel, the door, and the money
userStories.benefit: I can see conversion and revenue rather than only signups

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the analytics page, I see a registration funnel from registered to confirmed to checked in with step conversion, check-in rate over time, capacity-utilisation distribution, revenue over time split by free and paid, and a weekday by hour registration heatmap.

Given cohort mode, I see new versus returning attendees per cohort period with the definition of returning stated on the card; given insufficient data, the card states the minimum required instead of rendering empty axes.
Every chart card has a title, a one-line interpretation, a loading skeleton, an empty state, and a keyboard-reachable data-table alternative that exposes the same numbers.

userStories.title: Export what I am looking at
userStories.benefit: I can hand evidence to a sponsor, school, or teammate

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given any list or analytics view with an export action, the CSV contains the columns visible in that view, respects the active filters, includes a header row, and is named module-yyyy-MM-dd.csv.

Given any cell whose value begins with equals, plus, minus, at, tab, carriage return, or line feed, every field is double-quoted, internal quotes are doubled, and the dangerous leading character is neutralised per OWASP CSV-injection guidance; given a result set above the configured cap, the export is refused with the cap stated and a suggestion to narrow filters.
Given an export starts, its trigger shows progress and rejects repeat clicks; completion or failure raises a toast, and a failure names the reason without exposing a stack trace.

userStories.title: Produce a credible post-event report
userStories.benefit: organizers and sponsors receive an artifact they can trust

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given /admin/reports, I can choose an event and see attendance for confirmed, checked in, no-show, and cancelled, plus check-in rate over time, capacity utilisation, and revenue for paid events, with the data timestamp shown.

Given a report, I can export it as CSV and print or save it as PDF through a print stylesheet that removes admin chrome; given an event with no registrations, the report renders zeros plus an explanatory empty state.

userStories.title: Configure the platform, not just my account
userStories.benefit: the console reflects a global product instead of a Nigeria-only one

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given /admin/platform, a super admin can set default country, default currency as ISO 4217, default timezone as IANA, and toggle feature flags for command palette, reports, broadcasts, feedback inbox, and system health.

Given a super admin saves platform settings, the change persists in one settings document, writes a settings.updated audit entry containing before and after values, and affects formatting on the next render; a non-super-admin sees a read-only view and cannot reach the mutation.
Given maintenance mode is enabled, signed-out and non-admin visitors see a maintenance notice on public routes while admins retain access; enabling it requires typed confirmation and is audited.

userStories.title: Broadcast to a filtered audience
userStories.benefit: I can communicate without exporting addresses

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the broadcast composer, I choose an audience of all users, organizers with at least one event, attendees of a selected event, or admins, see the resolved recipient count before sending, and preview subject and body.

Given I send, the system requires typed confirmation, is rate-limited, sends through Resend in bounded batches, writes an announcement.sent audit entry with audience and count, and records per-recipient delivery outcomes.
Given delivery partially fails, the announcement shows sent and failed counts and its failures appear in system health; a partially failed send is never reported as a success.

userStories.title: Triage what users report
userStories.want: a queue of feedback and abuse reports
userStories.benefit: moderation is deliberate rather than reactive

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a signed-in non-admin submits feedback or reports an event from the public app, a validated record is created with type, optional target, message, and reporter; submission is rate-limited and duplicate submissions within the window are suppressed.

Given /admin/feedback, I can filter by status, type, and priority, open a record, add an internal note, move it through open to in review to resolved or dismissed, and see who changed it and when; every change writes an audit entry.
Given a record targets an event, I can open that event from the record; given the event was deleted, the record still renders with a target removed label.

userStories.title: Know whether the machinery is healthy
userStories.benefit: failures are caught before users report them

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given /admin/health, I see each cron job's last run and status, email delivery failures in 24 hours and 7 days, rate-limit rejections, and the age of open feedback; every signal states the window it covers.
Given a required server configuration value is missing, the panel lists it as unconfigured with the feature it affects, and never prints the value.
Given one health query fails, only that card shows an error with retry; the remaining cards stay usable.

userStories.title: Stop leaking attendee concepts into admin settings
userStories.want: settings to show only admin-relevant information
userStories.benefit: the console does not present attendee state as an admin task

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given /admin/settings, the Onboarding row is absent and no other attendee-only field such as interests or attendee location is rendered; profile identity, role, member-since, security actions, and notification preferences remain.
Given the settings query returns a record without admin-relevant fields, the page renders a degraded but truthful state instead of inventing Pending.

functionalRequirements.text: The admin shell MUST render navigation from one configuration source grouped as Overview, Audience, Events, Operations, Governance, and Personal.
The shell MUST mark the active route with aria-current, close the mobile drawer on route change, and restore focus to the drawer trigger.
Every admin page MUST render a shared page header with title, description, breadcrumb, and a primary-action slot.
The console MUST provide a command palette invoked by Ctrl/Cmd+K that searches pages, users, events, and registrations.
Palette search MUST run server-side behind an admin check, enforce a two-character minimum, debounce input, cap results per group, and return a typed result union.
The command palette MUST include deep-link quick actions permitted by the current role.
The dashboard MUST show trend cards for users, events, registrations, and estimated revenue, each with the named comparison window, delta, and sparkline.
The dashboard MUST derive an action queue from expiring invites, at-capacity events, stale open feedback, and failed email deliveries, each linking to its module.
The dashboard MUST show today's events with check-in progress, the ten most recent audit entries, and role-appropriate quick actions.
Every dashboard block MUST fetch independently so that one failure does not blank the page.
Analytics MUST accept one shared filter object covering date range, categories, countries, cities, ticket types, organizer, registration status, and check-in state.
Analytics MUST support preset and custom ranges, encode filters in the URL, and restore them on reload and history navigation.
Analytics MUST reject invalid ranges where start is after end or the span exceeds 730 days, and retain the last valid query.
Analytics MUST support previous-period comparison for every summary metric.
The analytics workspace MUST expose registration funnel, check-in trend, capacity utilisation, revenue split, cohort retention, and weekday by hour heatmap datasets.
Every chart MUST ship a data-table alternative exposing the same numbers.
Every analytics response MUST echo the applied filter and the row counts used to produce it.
Every list and report view MUST offer a CSV export of the current filtered dataset.
CSV generation MUST quote every field, double internal quotes, and neutralise formula-injection prefixes in accordance with OWASP guidance.
Exports MUST enforce a configurable row cap, be rate-limited per admin, and report progress, success, and failure.
The reports hub MUST list events and render a per-event report with attendance, check-in, capacity, and revenue sections plus a data timestamp.
Reports MUST be exportable as CSV and printable through a print stylesheet that hides admin chrome.
Platform settings MUST persist default country, currency, timezone, feature flags, and maintenance mode in a single document.
Platform settings writes MUST require super_admin and write a settings.updated audit entry with before and after values.
Maintenance mode MUST block public routes for non-admins while preserving admin access, and MUST require typed confirmation to enable.
Feature flags MUST hide a disabled module from navigation and reject its server queries.
Currency, date, number, and timezone formatting MUST derive from platform settings rather than hard-coded naira, NG, or a browser-local guess.
The broadcast composer MUST resolve and display recipient counts for all users, organizers, attendees of a selected event, and admins before sending.
Broadcast sending MUST require super_admin, typed confirmation, rate limiting, bounded Resend batches, and a persisted announcement record.
Broadcasts MUST record per-recipient delivery outcomes and expose sent and failed counts.
The announcements list MUST show status, audience, recipient counts, author, and timestamp.
The public app MUST let a signed-in non-admin submit feedback or report an event with validation, rate limiting, and duplicate suppression.
The feedback inbox MUST support status, type, and priority filters, a detail view, internal notes, status transitions, and navigation to the target.
Feedback mutations MUST require admin and write an audit entry for every status, priority, or note change.
A feedback record whose target was deleted MUST remain readable and labelled as target removed.
The health panel MUST report cron recency and status, 24-hour and 7-day email failures, rate-limit rejections, open-feedback age, and configuration presence.
Health reporting MUST expose only presence or absence of configuration, never a value.
Admin settings MUST NOT render hasCompletedOnboarding, interests, or attendee location.
The audit schema MUST add action and target literals for settings, announcements, feedback, exports, and maintenance mode.
All new Convex functions MUST declare convex/values argument validators and enforce role checks server-side.
The console MUST provide shared formatters for currency, compact numbers, relative time, percentages, and signed deltas.
The analytics and operational modules MUST add indexes so filtered windows are served by index ranges rather than full-collection scans.
Each major admin panel MUST sit behind a local error boundary with retry.
Day bucketing and report labels MUST use the platform timezone.
Every aggregated panel MUST display an as-of timestamp and the window it covers.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Every new Convex function MUST authenticate via Clerk and authorize with requireAdmin or a super-admin equivalent; client gating is defense in depth only.
Platform settings, broadcasts, and maintenance mode MUST be enforced as super_admin-only on the server, not only hidden in the UI.
Palette search, analytics queries, exports, broadcasts, feedback submission, and feedback mutations MUST be rate-limited through @convex-dev/rate-limiter and return a retry hint on rejection.
Every form MUST validate with Zod and every Convex function MUST declare convex/values validators; unvalidated free-form objects MUST NOT be accepted.
The feature MUST NOT introduce dangerouslySetInnerHTML; user-supplied feedback, notes, announcement bodies, and exported cells MUST be rendered or encoded as text.
Secrets MUST remain server-side; the health panel and settings UI MUST report presence only, and no .env file may be created or modified.
Production traffic MUST remain HTTPS-only with HSTS at the hosting layer; this feature MUST NOT weaken transport security.

Filtered analytics MUST return within 1.5 seconds p95 and the dashboard within 1 second p95 at 50,000 events and 500,000 registrations, using index ranges and bounded windows rather than collection scans.

Every new screen MUST meet WCAG 2.1 AA: visible focus, 4.5:1 text contrast, labelled controls, keyboard-complete palette and dialogs, chart data-table alternatives, and status messages announced without relying on colour.
Every new screen MUST be usable at 360px with no page-level horizontal scrolling; wide data tables MAY scroll inside their own container.
Every data-driven panel MUST provide loading, empty, and error states, with skeletons whose shape matches the final layout.
Motion MUST respect prefers-reduced-motion, and no animation may be required to understand a state change.
Exports MUST be capped at 10,000 rows by default, audited, rate-limited, and limited to the columns visible to the requesting admin.
TypeScript checking, ESLint with zero errors, and SpecDrive governance validation MUST pass before the feature is complete.
Every new administrative mutation MUST write an audit entry through logAdminAction, and failures MUST surface to the caller rather than being swallowed.
Feedback and announcement records MUST be retained until an explicit deletion, and every deletion MUST be audited.

edgeCases.description: The platform has zero users, events, and registrations.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The action queue shows a positive empty state and each analytics card states the minimum data it needs.

edgeCases.description: The comparison period has zero for a metric.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The delta renders new, with no division by zero.

edgeCases.description: A custom range starts after it ends or spans more than 730 days.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Inline validation is shown and the last valid query is retained.

edgeCases.description: A filter combination returns zero rows.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Per-chart empty states render, export is disabled, and filter chips remain removable.

edgeCases.description: An export exceeds the row cap.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The export is refused with the cap and a narrower-filter suggestion.

edgeCases.description: A CSV cell begins with equals, plus, minus, at, tab, carriage return, or line feed.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The field is quoted and the leading character is neutralised per OWASP guidance.

edgeCases.description: A non-super-admin opens platform settings or announcements.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The view is read-only or redirects and the mutation is rejected server-side.

edgeCases.description: Maintenance mode is enabled while an admin is mid-session.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Admins keep access and public visitors see the maintenance notice.

edgeCases.description: A broadcast audience resolves to zero recipients.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Send is disabled and the reason is shown.

edgeCases.description: Resend fails for some broadcast recipients.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: A partial-failure state is shown, failures appear in health, and success is not falsely reported.

edgeCases.description: A feedback record targets an event that was deleted.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The record remains readable and is labelled target removed.
An inline retry is offered, the dialog stays open, and nothing crashes.

edgeCases.description: Two admins resolve the same feedback record concurrently.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Both audit entries persist, the latest write wins, and the detail view refreshes.
Only that panel shows an error with retry.

edgeCases.description: A user has no name or avatar.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: An initials fallback and an email-based label render with no empty text node.

edgeCases.description: The platform settings document does not exist on first run.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Defaults render and the document is created on first save.

edgeCases.description: A timezone other than UTC is selected.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Day buckets, heatmap hours, and report labels follow it consistently and the active timezone is displayed.

edgeCases.description: A disabled feature flag is reached by direct URL.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: A not-enabled state renders and the server query rejects.

dependencies.name: Convex
dependencies.notes: Data, cron, rate limiter, and indexes.

risks.description: Read-on-demand analytics will not scale indefinitely.
risks.mitigation: Add indexes, clamp ranges, cap exports, and record the aggregate-pipeline trigger point in the plan.

risks.description: Broadcast email can damage sender reputation or spam users.
risks.mitigation: Super-admin only, typed confirmation, preview, rate limit, bounded batches, and a delivery log.

risks.description: Adding literals to the auditLogs unions is a schema change that can reject old documents if deployed out of order.
risks.mitigation: Deploy schema first, keep the validator exhaustive, and backfill no existing rows.
Admin-only, visible columns only, row cap, rate limit, and an audit entry per export.

risks.description: Maintenance mode can lock out legitimate operators.
risks.mitigation: Admin bypass, typed confirmation, audit entry, and a visible banner while active.

risks.description: The feedback form adds a public write surface.
risks.mitigation: Signed-in only, length caps, rate limit, duplicate suppression, and no file uploads.

risks.description: Timezone-aware bucketing changes existing chart values.
risks.mitigation: Display the active timezone on every affected card and document the change in the plan.

risks.description: Palette search adds a query per keystroke.
risks.mitigation: Two-character minimum, 250 ms debounce, per-group caps, and a rate limit.

risks.description: The scope is large for one version.
risks.mitigation: Phase delivery into milestones M0 through M4 so each is independently shippable.
